headline: A newspaper reporter got a US government information chatbot to hand out pasta recipes and sing about Elon Musk by hiding the requests inside a school quiz.
score_reason: Pool score kept: light, one-outlet test; the bot's origins are the paper's own description.
importance_line: A newspaper's informal test showed a topic-limited government chatbot can be steered off its brief, which matters to anyone relying on such limits, with the doubt that it is one outlet's test and the bot's backing is as the paper describes it.
summary: The Daily Star reports that its reporter got a chatbot called America, which the paper describes as a US government information bot built with Google and Elon Musk's SpaceXAI, to give pasta recipes and sing about Musk by first asking for a school quiz and then slipping the recipe in as a joke answer. It is the paper's own informal test, but it shows how a narrowly limited chatbot can be sidestepped with an innocent-looking request.
notes: Read full Daily Star text. Bot origin (Google, SpaceXAI) is attributed to the paper, not checked.
